q: How should a Morbi tile maker count the clay, frit and glaze it buys?
title: Morbi tiles: bought clay, frit and glaze
short: Clay, feldspar, frit, glaze and packaging are purchased goods, Scope 3 category 1. Take tonnes from the invoices and use supplier or named database factors. Kiln gas and power stay in Scope 1 and 2, and transport to the plant is category 4.
audience: Wall, floor and vitrified tile makers in the Morbi cluster of Gujarat

p: Frit and glaze by kg, each with its supplier.
Cartons and pallets by unit or kg.
Frit is itself melted at high temperature before you buy it, so its factor per kg matters. Ask the frit maker for their figure before using a generic one.

senseible: Senseible reads the energy invoices behind the making stage into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, and keeps material invoices on the Scope 3 trail. Material factors come from your supplier or a named database and are labelled with their source, so the product figure can be traced line by line.
